name: jm-live-skip
description: JudgeMySite: run a live Full Trial and INTERRUPT it — take the mid-show 'read the verdict now' exit the moment the ruling lands. The second worked example, and the one that shows the shape jm-full-trial.json cannot: a flow whose whole point is to interrupt the thing it started, because the code under test only runs on the abort path.

steps.comment: The submit button is ABSENT from the a11y tree until the URL field is non-empty — it renders disabled. Hence it is matched here, after the fill, not before.

Wait for the SKIP BANNER, not the verdict page. The server emits its verdict event the instant synthesis returns — before the visual drain — and that gap is the only window in which the skip exists. Budget is generous because a deployment with a changed runner bundle re-bakes its golden snapshot first (60-270s) on top of the trial itself.
steps.match: The ruling is in|bench has reached its verdict

steps.comment: THE STEP UNDER TEST. This click aborts the client stream mid-show, which is what kills the Lambda and is exactly why the teardown had to be moved into after(). A hard failure here is correct: if the button cannot be resolved, no abort happened, and any later 'teardown works' reading would be about a run that never skipped.
Bring the verdict surfaces into frame so the tape carries them: FIRST ORDER band, then the charges with their receipts.
